name: SpaceX
day_summary: SPCX never gave the dip-buyers their entry. Instead of the expected Day 3-5 float-normalization fade into $130-145, the stock pressed higher again — trading ~$177.99 intraday, up ~+11% on the day off the $160.95 debut close and now ~+35% over the two sessions since IPO (and ~+32% over the $135 offer). The fuel: MSCI early-inclusion passive buying (live since June 13) colliding with a ~4% float, on top of a screaming risk-on tape — Trump declared the US–Iran peace deal 'now complete,' the Strait of Hormuz is reopening, oil is tumbling, S&P +1.49% (~7,542), Nasdaq +2.38%. Bulls won again; the float-normalization entry plan was overrun by the same forced-demand mechanic the thesis identified.
long_pnl: +~35% for IPO allocants ($135 → ~$177.99) and +~11% for anyone who held the $160.95 debut close — the structural float/MSCI bid is paying the longs
short_pnl: n/a — still no borrow, no listed chain, no short interest; bears remain spectators pointing at the ~94x revenue multiple

decision.rationale: Be honest about the plan: the float-normalization thesis told us to wait for a Day 3-5 dip into $130-145 — and that dip never came. The MSCI passive bid into a ~4% float, amplified by a risk-on tape, drove SPCX to ~$178 instead. Chasing ~+35% two days into a record IPO, well above the planned $130-145 entry and with no fundamental anchor until ~Sept 2, is poor risk/reward. The disciplined call stays HOLD/WAIT at low conviction: allocants ride a core and may trim into strength; new money does NOT chase $178. Let the passive bid exhaust and look for the first real pullback toward $150-160 (the open/debut-close shelf) rather than re-anchoring to the offer. A daily close back under $135 would re-open the original $130-145 entry; a close under $118 invalidates the long thesis entirely. Keep size ~2%.

what_traders_are_doing: The float-normalization crowd is caught flat-footed — the planned $130-145 dip never materialized because the MSCI passive bid plus a risk-on melt-up pushed SPCX to ~$178. Allocants up ~35% are taking partial profits into strength while holding a core for the index-inclusion runway. Disciplined new money is standing down rather than chasing two days into a record IPO. Momentum desks are riding the ~4%-float squeeze, fully aware it cuts both ways. Skeptics still have no vehicle to express a short and are simply flagging the ~104x revenue multiple at a ~$1.9T cap. The honest desk posture: respect the move, do not chase it, wait for the first real pullback.

outlook.short_term: Squeeze-driven and stretched. The MSCI passive bid into a ~4% float, supercharged by the Iran-peace risk-on melt-up, pushed SPCX to ~$178 and denied the planned $130-145 dip. Two days in, +35% off the offer with no fundamental anchor until ~Sept 2 is a chase, not a setup. Expect sharp two-way swings as passive demand exhausts and momentum money rotates; the first real test is whether $160 (the debut close) holds as support on a pullback. New money waits for $150-160 or a return toward $135 rather than paying $178. FOMC June 17 is the macro gate; Juneteenth June 19 thins liquidity.
outlook.long_term: Unchanged from Day 1: a real space/satellite megacap — Starlink (5M+ subs, ~40% growth), Starship, Starshield — but now priced even richer (~104x 2025 revenue at ~$1.9T) for a 2029-2032 outcome. The structural float/passive-inclusion bid is a powerful near-term tailwind, but it is a supply-and-demand phenomenon, not a fundamental one; the multiple still demands flawless execution. Earnings ~Sept 2 is the first moment the story has to print numbers, and the ~December 2026 lock-up expiry is the first major supply event. Long-term bulls (Baron, Rinehart) are positioned for the decade — patient, sized, and unbothered by the two-day pop.

analysis:
## The dip never came

The plan was to wait for the **Day 3-5 float-normalization dip** into **$130-145**. It never arrived. Instead SPCX [jumped a second day, now up over 35% since debut](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-stock-jumps-for-second-day-now-up-over-35-since-debut-143317444.html), trading **~$177.99** intraday — up **~+11%** off the $160.95 close and **~+32%** over the $135 offer. The reason is the exact mechanic the thesis flagged, just stronger than expected: **MSCI early-inclusion passive buying** (live since June 13) into a **~4% float** overwhelmed flipper supply. [TradingKey notes SPCX cleared the 0.236 Fib at $170.19](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/261967404-spacex-stock-forecast-after-a-19-percent-ipo-surge-can-spcx-keep-climbing-before-earnings-tradingkey) on conviction buying.

## A risk-on tailwind on top

The macro tape did the rest. [Trump declared the US–Iran peace deal 'now complete', the Strait of Hormuz is reopening and oil is tumbling](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/6/15/stock-markets-soar-oil-falls-as-us-iran-confirm-deal-to-end-war): **S&P +1.49% (~7,542), Nasdaq +2.38%, Dow +1.20%**. High-beta growth and 'investable space' rode the wave; Musk-proxies broadly caught a bid.

## Respect the move, don't chase it

Here is the honest read: bulls won again, but the disciplined call is still **HOLD/WAIT at low conviction**. Buying **~+35% two days into a record IPO**, well above the planned **$130-145** entry and at **~104x** revenue with no earnings until **~Sept 2**, is a chase. Allocants up ~35% can trim into strength and hold a core for the index runway; new money waits for the first real pullback toward **$150-160** (the debut-close shelf) — or a close back under **$135**, which re-opens the original plan entry. A daily close under **$118** invalidates the long. The squeeze is real and powerful, but it is supply-and-demand, not fundamentals — and **FOMC June 17** plus the ~December lock-up are the events that can turn a thin-float melt-up into a thin-float reversal.
